method: Flesch-Kincaid grade with a transparent vowel-group syllable heuristic; estimated age = grade + 5, floored at zero. Count sentences using terminal punctuation. Exact measured corpora included. This is a rough editorial screen, not a learner assessment. Teacher-only text excluded.

corpora.text: I can share my part in our made-up story. I can use a start and end cue. I can share or direct my real part. I can log what I did and who saw it. Our story is made up. Pick act, speak, sign or direct. Our audience is our class and invited staff only. Find our real story plan. Show first, next and last. Try the start cue once. Watch the two class examples. See a clear start. See the change and the end. Which cue helps us? Agree first, next and last. Give each person a real part. Try a start and end cue. Keep our own space. Share our short story. Use your chosen role and cue. You may share with just one class member or invited staff member. A watcher says: I notice ___. Keep a note of your real part. Say what you really shared. Who watched or listened? What did they really notice? Store your plan and note. I shared / directed ___. My audience was ___. I chose ___ because ___. Keep my real work for tomorrow. A made-up set of events. A sign to start or stop. The people who watch or listen. Your part in a story.

Pick a role or direct the adult. Use first, next and last hand pictures. Share with one class member or invited staff member. Tell or show your real part. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Use our real three-part story plan. Share your part with clear start and end cues. Ask one watcher what they noticed. Log what you did, who watched and your choice. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Do the same core share. Make the change and new plan clear. Use a calm cue to help the group. Explain one choice and keep real feedback. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

First the group point to a big space. Next they show that the space is small. Last they make a small roof with their hands. A hand cue helps them hold each picture for three counts. What comes first? What comes last? Which cue could help us share our story? One voice says, We want a den. Next a voice says, The space is small. Last a voice says, We can make a small den. Each person stays in their own space. Which line tells us the change? Would you use a voice, a hand cue or both? Why? I notice ___. I could use ___ in my own scene because ___. These are invented class models. They are not pupil work.

Point wide. Say: We want a den. Give a calm start cue. Bring hands close. Say: The space is small. Hold for three comfortable counts. Make a small roof with hands. Say: We can make a small den. Give an end cue and relax. Ask a real watcher to name one feature. Use the safe plan you agreed. Share with the class and invited staff only. Show your real role. Keep a note of what you did. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Date __________________  Lesson ART_BUILD_S2_W05_P1 Art form __________________  My role __________________ Today I performed / directed / chose to pass ___. My real part was ___. My audience was ___. I chose ___ because ___. The watcher noticed ___ / no feedback yet. Help I used was ___. If pending, my next action is ___. My work or note is kept at __________________ Help I used __________________ I wrote my words / an adult wrote for me. I checked them. Keep my real work from today. A photo is a choice.

Perform our drama (World Book Day link). I can use a start and end cue. I can share or direct my real part. I can log what I did and who saw it. story: A made-up set of events. cue: A sign to start or stop. audience: The people who watch or listen. role: Your part in a story. Use a made-up story. Keep your own space. Stop on the open hand. You can sit, stay silent or direct. You may share with just the adult.

I can say what I did and sort my real arts-log work. I can name one drama skill I used. I can show my own work and choice. I can mark a gap and a next step. Find your real plan and share note. You can point, speak, sign or draw. A gap is okay. We will plan a next step. Point to a skill: cue, pose or voice. Which one did you really use or direct? Show the real note if you have it. See a teacher review example. A real note shows what happened. A blank space means not yet. What would we do next? Sort one real class example. A: take part. B: explore. C: create. D: share. What is real? What is pending? In your arts log, review your real work. A: what did I do? B: what did I notice? C: what did I make or change? D: what did I share? Name one skill and one choice. Mark any gap: pending. Add a next step. Check the list with an adult. Does it show my own work? Are dates and audience real? Keep the real items together. My skill was ___. My choice was ___ because ___. My next step is ___. My arts log shows my real work. Something you can get better at. Look back at what you did. Real work or a note of what happened. One thing to try next.

Look at one real item with an adult. Point: did it happen or is it pending? Sort under A, B, C or D with help. Say or show one skill and a next step. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Sort your real work under A, B, C and D. Name your part, choice and a reason. Check dates, audience and help used. Mark each gap pending and add a next action. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Complete the same real evidence list. Use two real items to show a skill change. Explain which choice helped your story. Choose a small next skill goal and how to check it. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

First the group point to a big space. Next they show that the space is small. Last they make a small roof with their hands. A hand cue helps them hold each picture for three counts. What comes first? What comes last? Which cue could help us share our story? One voice says, We want a den. Next a voice says, The space is small. Last a voice says, We can make a small den. Each person stays in their own space. Which line tells us the change? Would you use a voice, a hand cue or both? Why? I notice ___. I could use ___ in my own scene because ___. These are invented class models. They are not pupil work.

Point to a teacher model of a real role note. Say: This tells what I did. Point to a blank share record. Say: I do not know that a share happened. It is pending. Sort the real note under A. Keep a planned share separate from D. Say: My next action is to ask for a quiet share with a class member or invited staff. Review the scene. Keep real feedback. Find your own arts-log items. Choose one skill to keep or practise next. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

My work or note is kept at __________________ Help I used __________________ I wrote my words / an adult wrote for me. I checked them. Keep my real work from today. A photo is a choice.

Reflect on my drama skills; arts-log evidence. I can name one drama skill I used. I can show my own work and choice. I can mark a gap and a next step. skill: Something you can get better at. review: Look back at what you did. evidence: Real work or a note of what happened. next step: One thing to try next. Use a made-up story. Keep your own space. Stop on the open hand. You can sit, stay silent or direct. You may share with just the adult.

I can share my own part in a short performance for our allowed audience. I can use my agreed role and cues. I can perform or direct for a real class or invited staff audience. I can record my own part and real feedback. Our audience is our class and invited staff only. Choose perform, sign, speak or direct. A quiet private share is an option. Find our real outline and skill plan. Name your part and a cue. If a plan is missing, make a short fresh one. Compare the two invented class examples. Notice a start, change, response and end. Which cue helps an audience follow? Choose one skill to use today. Agree our roles and cues. Try one calm run. Ask a listener to notice one skill. Keep the story and the audience clear. Share our short performance. Use your own role and chosen skill. You may share privately within our class and invited staff. Ask for one real notice. Keep your own part in the arts log. Name your actual contribution. What did the listener really notice? What choice would you keep? Store your plan and feedback for Wednesday. Log what you really performed or directed. Record the actual date and audience. Keep your own choice and reason. If pending, name one next action. The people who watch or listen. A sign for a start, pause or end. Your own part in shared work. A useful notice about what happened.

Pick a small role or direct an adult. Use our four short story parts. Share with one class member or invited staff member. Confirm your real part and one choice. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Use the actual story outline and your role. Share with clear cues for the allowed audience. Ask one listener to notice a skill. Log your part, actual audience, choice and real feedback. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Complete the same core share. Help the group use a clear pause and end cue. Explain how a chosen skill helps the audience. Optional next level: check one real skill goal and keep your own view of the result. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

The group plan wide moves. The imagined space gets smaller. A planner asks for ideas. The group test small hand moves, choose one and end together. A narrator uses short lines to mark the change and the new plan. What makes the change and response clear? How could a short line or pause help our audience? The group begin with wide hand poses. A point to the word Change marks a smaller space. Each offers a small move. They choose one and repeat it together, then hold a final pose. The intended meaning is explained after the share. How does the group show a choice without speech? Which feature would you keep in your own piece, and why? I notice ___. I could use ___ in my own scene because ___. These are invented class models. They are not pupil work.

Use a calm start cue and safe wide hand poses for the first plan. Show close hands. Say: Our imagined space is smaller. Pause. Offer a small wave and repeat the chosen move together. Hold a comfortable final pose, relax and ask the present listener about one feature. Use the safe plan you agreed. Share with the class and invited staff only. Show your real role. Keep a note of what you did. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

My chosen skill and reason were ___. My actual audience and date were ___. The listener really noticed ___ / no feedback yet. My own view of the result is ___. Help I used was ___. Pending item and next action: ___. My work or note is kept at __________________ Help I used __________________ I wrote my words / an adult wrote for me. I checked them. Keep my real work from today. A photo is a choice.

Use your real skill goal. After the share, say what happened. Which choice helped? What would you try next? You can speak, point or draw. Keep your own goal, real practice note, actual share and your own view. Keep feedback only if it happened.

I can review my real contribution and check my arts-log evidence. I can use real evidence to review my skill. I can check A, B, C and D and mark gaps honestly. I can give my own view and one next action. Find the actual plan, trial and share note. Use your own work and words. Missing evidence stays pending. Name one real skill or choice. Find the item that helps show it. Which words are your own view? See a teacher evidence review. A real item supports a claim. A plan is not proof it happened. What should stay pending? Check one real item under A, B, C or D. Say what it shows and whose work it is. Check actual date, audience and support. Mark a gap and next action. Review your real performance or direction. Check A Take part, B Explore, C Create and D Share. Give your own view and reason. Mark gaps pending. Add a next action. Optional next level: check your real skill plan, practice and learning. Read your evidence list with an adult. Can you find each real item? Does each gap have a next action? Keep your own words and real records together. My skill changed or stayed ___ because ___. My own view is ___. My next action is ___. My list keeps real work and honest gaps. Look back at real work and choices. Work or a clear note of what really happened. Your own view of what you did and learned. Still to do or check.

Check one real item at a time with an adult. Point to A, B, C or D, or pending. Say or show one real skill choice. Confirm your own view and a next action. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Check your real A, B, C and D evidence. Review your actual role, skill and feedback. Give your own view with a reason. Mark gaps pending and list exact next actions. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Complete the same honest evidence review. Compare two actual trials or choices. Explain your view of what helped the audience. Optional next level: check real skill goals, practice, learning and the next action. In your book or arts log, show your own part. I chose ___ because ___. I will try ___ next. You can point, sign, speak, draw or ask an adult to write your words.

Show a labelled teacher plan to share. Say: This is a plan, not proof of an audience. Show a real teacher role note. Say what the note actually supports. Check A, B, C and D. Mark the missing share or feedback pending. Add a next action and an own-view sentence. Keep optional skill evidence only where real. Review the scene. Keep real feedback. Find your own arts-log items. Choose one skill to keep or practise next. The adult model is an example. Your arts log must show your real choice.

Check your real skill plan and practice. What did you try? What changed? Give your own view and reason. Say what you learned and one next step. Keep real plans, trials, changes and your own words. Add real feedback or sharing notes if you have them. Mark gaps pending and add the next action.
